cim: Nvidia opens investigation after reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
cim_eredeti: Nvidia opens investigation after reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Wall Street will be looking to bounce back after a very tough day for tech companies on Thursday that saw shares of Amazon, Intel and Google’s parent company Alphabet plummet. It comes as the crypto industry suffered the biggest heist in history with hackers making off with nearly $6 billion in cryptocurrency. NBC’s Brian Cheung reports for TODAY.

The board of Nvidia on Sunday said that it was opening an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

The announcement followed reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese business woman whom the outlets reported had been recruited to spy for China. The two are not related.

Stream NBC4 newscasts for free right here, right now.

NBC News has not confirmed either report and has reached out to the Trump administration for comment.

“The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company said in a statement.

“A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”

The company added that it “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.”

In memo to Nvidia employees shared by the company with NBC News, Huang said: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.”

The New York Times and the Financial Times reported that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen whose Singapore-based company was buying Nvidia’s advanced chips, had been under surveillance by U.S. intelligence agencies. Those agencies, the reports said, found that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China’s top intelligence agency.

Jensen Huang and Nvidia, for years, have been at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom. Nvidia’s products are the most highly-sought after chips in the world, however its top-tier products are mostly restricted from being sold to customers in China due to national security fears.

Huang essentially serves as an ambassador for the industry, regularly appearing alongside the likes of President Donald Trump, King Charles, and at conference to tout his company and what he says will be immense payoff in the future from AI.

In the latest series of these reports, published on Sunday afternoon by the New York Times, the paper reported that concerns inside the U.S. government about Alice Huang and Jensen Huang rose as high as involving Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

On Friday, the FT reported that the U.S government believed that wJensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang. In response to that story, the FT reported that Nvidia declined to comment and said that Jensen Huang meets “thousands of customer executives every year” as any CEO normally does.

“To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust,” Huang’s memo said.

The email to employees continued: “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.”

A spokesperson for Nvidia told NBC News that “today’s news will not slow” the company and that Huang was “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.”
